summary:
TerraFertility is an interactive agro-climatic web dashboard that leverages real-time NASA satellite data to forecast soil health and optimize crop rotations.
To solve the challenge, our platform integrates NASA POWER API telemetry (MERRA-2, GPM, CERES) to calculate a dynamic Soil Fertility Index for any geographic location. It simulates 20-year soil degradation scenarios, comparing traditional monoculture against sustainable practices like No-Till and scientific crop rotation. Based on these metrics, the system generates actionable agronomic reports and recommends the top-3 crops for soil recovery.
This project is crucial because traditional farming accelerates topsoil exhaustion and carbon loss. TerraFertility bridges the gap between complex aerospace data and everyday farmers, empowering them to transition to regenerative agriculture, prevent desertification, and ensure long-term food security without expensive laboratory tests.
details:
What it does & How it works: TerraFertility is a satellite-driven agro-climatic intelligence platform designed to restore soil health and plan long-term crop rotations. The system allows users to target any agricultural parcel on an interactive satellite map and retrieves real-time agroclimatology telemetry via the NASA POWER API (MERRA-2, GPM, and CERES). By processing daily temperature, precipitation, and solar irradiance, our model computes a dynamic Soil Fertility Index and simulates soil organic carbon (SOC) trajectories across a 20-year horizon (2026–2046) under three distinct agricultural practices: conventional moldboard plowing, scientific crop rotation, and regenerative No-Till farming.

Benefits & Expected Impact: The platform eliminates the need for expensive preliminary soil laboratory tests by delivering immediate, satellite-backed audits. It empowers farmers to mitigate land degradation and topsoil wind/water erosion, optimize water retention during extreme heat stress, and reduce chemical fertilizer dependence through biological nitrogen fixation. The long-term impact is combating desertification and supporting climate-resilient agriculture while increasing farmer profitability.

Tools, Languages, & Software:

  • Languages & Architecture: Pure semantic HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+ client-side architecture).
  • Styling & Design System: Tailored UI inspired by the official NASA Web Design System.
  • Geospatial & Visualization: Leaflet.js with Esri World Imagery satellite basemaps, and Chart.js for 20-year predictive mathematical modeling.
  • APIs & Telemetry: Direct integration with the NASA POWER API (Agroclimatology community archive).

Creativity & Key Considerations: The creativity lies in transforming complex aerospace astrophysics and raw satellite telemetry into an accessible, interactive time-lapse simulator. Farmers can visually advance a timeline slider from 2026 to 2046 to witness how sustainable tillage preserves soil carbon versus how monoculture depletes it. Our team specifically accounted for regional aridity stress, hydrothermal coefficients, crop-specific nutrient extraction penalties, and seamless multi-language accessibility.
